name: Blue Topaz
physical: Traditionally associated with ease in the throat and neck
Said to bring a cool, refreshing calm
Crystal healers link it with relaxation after long days of talking
summary: Blue Topaz is a cool, sparkling gem, almost always treated, linked in crystal lore with calm, honest communication and a clear throat chakra.
intro: Blue topaz is the sparkling, ocean-toned gem that fills jewelry cases from sky blue to deep inky shades. Natural blue topaz exists but is quite rare and pale, so nearly all of the blue on the market starts as colourless crystal that is irradiated and then heated. The trade names tell you the shade: sky blue is the lightest, Swiss blue is a vivid mid tone and London blue is the dark, steely teal. Despite its man-made colour, the stone is real topaz, hard, clear and brilliant, and perfectly stable. It is affordable, available in large sizes and offers impressive clarity for the price.
history: Topaz has been prized since antiquity, and blue examples were noted in pegmatites in Russia's Urals and in Brazil. The technique of turning colourless topaz blue by irradiation and heating was developed in the twentieth century, and it transformed the gem trade by making a rare colour widely available. Colour-treated blue topaz became popular in the 1970s and 1980s, and it is now a major gemstone. It is a modern December birthstone and a traditional gem of the fourth anniversary. Texas has even named topaz its state gem, with blue stones commonly cut from the Mason County crystals.
meaning: In the crystal tradition blue topaz is a stone of clear communication and peaceful honesty. Its sky colour is tied to the throat chakra, and practitioners suggest it for anyone who wants to speak with confidence but also with kindness. It is said to cool a quick temper and settle an agitated mind, making it popular with speakers, teachers, customer-service staff and anyone in a talkative job. Some healers also use it for calm reflection, as a stone that invites a deep breath. Because the colour comes from treatment, some practitioners remark that it is a stone about transformation, a clear thing made blue. Physically it is traditionally associated with ease in the throat and a cooling sense of relaxation.
howToUse: Wear a blue topaz pendant to meetings, presentations or any day with plenty of conversation. In meditation, hold the stone at the base of the throat and breathe slowly, picturing a clear blue sky. Keep a piece on the desk to support honest emails and calm decision making. Place one beside the bed to wind down, or use it in a communication grid with clear quartz and blue lace agate. Because it is so affordable, it is easy to give as a gift to friends who are starting a new venture.
care: Blue topaz can be washed with lukewarm water and a soft cloth, or cleansed with smoke, sound or moonlight. Keep it away from steam and ultrasonic cleaners, and avoid sudden temperature changes, as topaz has a cleavage that can split under thermal or physical shock. The colour from irradiation is stable in sunlight, but some very pale natural stones can fade, so brief sun charging is fine. Store separately in a soft pouch.
identify: Blue topaz is hard and heavy for its size, and it scratches quartz. Colour is almost always created by irradiation and heat, which is accepted if disclosed. Look-alikes include aquamarine, blue glass, synthetic spinel and blue apatite. Aquamarine tends to be lighter and less intense, while topaz often has a stronger, bolder blue. Mystic topaz and coated stones carry a rainbow surface treatment that can wear away. Ask for treatment information and keep receipts for higher-priced pieces.

faq.a: The mineral is natural topaz, but the blue colour on most stones comes from irradiation and heat applied to colourless crystals. This process is permanent, standard in the trade and stable under normal wear.
Crystal tradition links it with calm, honest speech and a clear throat chakra. People wear it to communicate with confidence, ease tension in conversation and invite a peaceful, clear mind.

faq.q: What is the difference between Swiss and London blue?
faq.a: These are trade shades. Sky blue is the palest, Swiss blue is a bright, vivid mid-tone and London blue is a deep, darker teal-blue. All are treated colourless topaz, with price depending on size and depth of colour.
